purpose: WP39. refinement_role_v1 (WP34) found that the four posteriordb models where oWALNUTS is furthest behind CmdStan per gradient are exactly those where the reverse-coarsening check ends the most transitions (10-54 % of retained transitions), while the check's own gradient cost is negligible (target_calls_reverse < 1 % of retained calls). The cost is orbit truncation: the failed doubling is discarded and the orbit ends early. ReverseCoarserPolicy::ZeroWeightBeyond (kernel commit e5a6617, research-only) keeps the failed leaf's endpoint and every leaf beyond it in that direction at zero weight and lets the orbit run on; selection is restricted to states connected to the current one through passing leaves, so the transition stays exact (tests/reverse_coarser_policy.rs). Does it pay per gradient on posteriordb, and is it exact on the funnel?

arms.stop: Tuning::default() + Adaptation::default(): ReverseCoarserPolicy::StopOrbit, the shipped sampler (bit-identical to refinement_role_v1's `da` at equal seeds)

common: Tuning::default() (h0 0.5, depth 10, min_micro_steps 1, eight refinement levels, delta 1, MomentumSum, divergence threshold 1000); Adaptation::default() (dual averaging 0.8 on the coarse-endpoint statistic, Stan regularisation, DEFAULT_WARMUP_EXHAUSTION); Metric::diagonal(); Init::uniform(); Limits::admit_worst_case(); four threads; cached initial evaluation; no per-model tuning; no source change between arms

external.what: BridgeStan 2.9.0 libraries compiled without STAN_THREADS for posteriordb_bench_v6 (models/) and its posteriordb checkout; reused, not recompiled

cmdstan_reference: posteriordb_bench_v5 artifacts (CmdStan 2.39.0 defaults, seeds 87101-87103), cited not rerun
run_order: models in listed order; arms stop then beyond; seeds ascending; strictly sequential; then the funnel rows for both arms

side_checks.funnel: Neal's 10-D funnel at the sampler defaults plus the arm's policy: 4 x 2,000 / 20,000, starts omega in {-3, -1, 1, 3}, per-seed MCSE z of P(omega < -5) (exact 0.0478), gate |z| <= 2 on every seed for `beyond` (and reported for `stop`); src/bin/funnel.rs

predictions.P1: beyond has zero reverse-coarser stops on every cell (by construction) and continued-leaf counts equal to stop's rejection counts within seed noise; adapted h within 0.95-1.05x of stop's on every model (the acceptance statistic does not see the zero-weight leaves)
predictions.P2: on the four target models beyond is 1.15-2.0x stop per gradient, largest on accel_gp (rc stop 54 % in WP34) and smallest on the noncentered eight schools (10 %); leaves per orbit rise by 1/(1 - rc stop) or less
predictions.P3: on the thirteen control models (rc stop 0.8-7 %) beyond is within 0.95-1.05x of stop; the geomean over 17 lands at 1.05-1.20
predictions.P4: funnel |z| <= 2 on every seed for both arms; beyond's omega ESS per call within 0.9-1.2x of stop's
predictions.P5: gates: beyond passes at least as many of the 51 cells as stop; max rank R-hat and |z| against the reference unchanged in distribution
predictions.risk: the zero-weight tail can make orbits run to the depth cap on the target models (WP34: accel_gp depth histogram concentrated at 9-10); if depth-cap stops rise above 20 % of transitions on a model the per-gradient gain there will be below P2 and this is the mechanism to report

decision_rules_text: flip the sampler default to ZeroWeightBeyond iff C1 geomean of the per-model seed-median ratio (beyond/stop of min bulk ESS per gradient, all target calls) over 17 models >= 1.10, C2 no model < 0.90, C3 beyond passes >= as many gates as stop over the 51 cells, C4 funnel |z| <= 2 on every seed for beyond, C5 geomean over the four target models >= 1.15. Otherwise: keep StopOrbit as the default and the opt-in stays research-only. Report all cells; no reruns; failures are results; nothing tuned after seeing results.
seed_provenance: grep-verified unused in the repository (outside vendored site-packages) before the freeze
